# Verify user token

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:identity-verification` · **Epic:** [#20](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/20) · **Tickets:** 7 (2S 5M)

The worker reads a user token from Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT, or from X-Warden-Identity on HTTP that Warden terminates (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2). It verifies the token against the issuer's JWKS and strips both headers before forwarding, in every mode. It then records sub, verified email, groups and identity status on every event, receipt, decision log and fleet event. Each agent's identity mode is off (the default) or attribute. Attribute mode records identity and never blocks. Only status valid produces a policy subject, so later group and user rules can never match an unverified caller.

## How we build it

- New package `internal/identity` (no such package exists yet; go.mod gains `github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3` pinned to a release at least two weeks old). It defines `Claims{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, GroupsTruncated, SID, Issuer, AZP, Nonce, IssuedAt, Expiry}`, the policy subject `Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID}` with `SubjectFrom(claims, status) *Subject` (nil unless status is valid; p1-group-policy, p1-block-list and later per-user features use this one type), `Status` (off|none|valid|invalid|expired|unverified|conflict), a bounded `Reason` (bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, wrong_azp, unknown_kid, alg_not_allowed, malformed, too_large, ttl_too_long, jwks_unavailable), the interface `Verifier.Verify(ctx, raw string, opts ...VerifyOption) (Claims, Status, Reason)` and `StripHeaders(http.Header)`, which deletes X-Warden-Identity and Proxy-Authorization. A fake verifier lives in test/fakes.
- OIDC verifier. `NewOIDCVerifier(Config{Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, ClockSkew, MaxTokenTTL, GroupsClaim, AllowInsecureIssuer, CAFile})` does no network I/O at construction. Discovery (when JWKSURL is empty) and JWKS fetches happen lazily. They use a dedicated http.Client with Proxy=nil, a plain net.Dialer (not the proxy SafeDialer, so an issuer on a private network such as Dex on cp-net is reachable, like newControlPlaneHTTPClient in internal/worker/wiring.go), a 5s timeout and a capped response body. A Warden wrapper around the go-oidc key set allows at most one unknown-kid refetch per 30s per issuer (singleflight plus an interval floor) and keeps the last good keyset while fetches fail. Warden enforces this itself and does not rely on go-oidc to limit refetches. Allowed algorithms are exactly RS256 and ES256. The verifier checks iss exactly, checks that aud contains Audience, and checks azp against AllowedAZP when that list is set. exp and nbf are checked in Warden with ClockSkew (default 60s, max 5m), and exp-iat must not exceed MaxTokenTTL (default 1h). Tokens over 16 KiB are rejected before parsing. Groups are read from GroupsClaim (default `groups`), sorted, de-duplicated and capped at 64 entries of 256 bytes, with GroupsTruncated set. Email is lowercased and kept only when email_verified is not false. A bounded LRU (10k entries) keyed by sha256(token) caches results until min(exp, now+5m), and exp is re-checked on every hit. `WithNonce` lets the CP console login (W-P1-SSO-03) reuse the verifier with its own audience.
- Config. `SettingsWire.Identity *IdentitySettings{DefaultMode, Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, GroupsClaim, ClockSkewSeconds, MaxTokenTTLSeconds, AllowInsecureIssuer}` (json `identity`, omitempty; absent means off). A matching local `identity:` YAML block serves standalone workers. Per-agent override is a new `Identity string` field added to both the existing `AgentSettings` and `config.AgentPolicy` (and rawAgent), so the existing `AgentSettings(a)` conversion in SettingsWireFromPolicy keeps compiling. A worker resolves its mode for the agent ID that `worker.defaultAgentID` already computes (Agents[0].ID, or `agent:<port>` via agentid.PortBindingIdentifier). Validation on the CP and locally accepts off|attribute and rejects `require` with a 'Phase 2' error; a worker's parseRemotePolicy does not reject a served wire for an unsupported mode, which W-P1-VRFY-07 handles by keeping the previous identity config. An http issuer is rejected unless allowInsecureIssuer is set. The block holds no secrets.
- Hot reload. The verifier lives in a new atomic holder `identityP` on Proxy (same pattern as secretsP and judgeP). The SettingsApplier rebuilds the verifier only when the issuer, audience, JWKS URL, azp, skew or TTL settings change, so the key cache survives unrelated applies. If a rebuild fails, or a newer CP sends an unknown mode, the worker keeps the previous identity config and logs one warning. In-flight connections keep their snapshot.
- Extraction. `handleConn` (internal/proxy/serve.go) captures Proxy-Authorization in its existing CONNECT header loop: Basic with username `session` (the password is the token) or Bearer. Any other form gives status invalid with reason malformed. Verification runs before `Policy.Evaluate`, so CONNECT deny events are attributed too. The result is a per-connection `connIdentity{Claims, Status, Reason, Expiry}` passed to handleTLS, tunnel, handleHTTP and handleGRPC. The worker consumes the CONNECT request, so this header is never forwarded today. X-Warden-Identity: Bearer is honored only on HTTP that Warden terminates. For HTTP/1.1 a new `identityStage` runs in runRequestStages right after readRequest and before judgeGate, so the judge, DLP and the secret swap never see the token. For HTTP/2 the same resolver runs at the top of `serveGRPCStream` (internal/proxy/grpc.go), before the swap and before copyGRPCHeaders. Raw tunnels (no CA, non-TLS traffic, unknown protocols inside TLS) are opaque: they carry only the CONNECT identity, and the worker logs one startup warning when attribute mode is on and no CA is configured.
- Stripping is unconditional and is the one deliberate exception to default-off. `identity.StripHeaders` runs on every terminated HTTP/1.1 request and every h2 stream, in every mode, including when there are no identity settings. A user token therefore never reaches an upstream from traffic Warden terminates.
- Status rules in attribute mode never block a request. A valid CONNECT identity applies to the connection until its exp (plus skew) passes; later requests on that connection get status expired. A per-request header applies when CONNECT carried no token. Two valid identities with different sub give status conflict and no subject, and the request proceeds; a 403 identity_conflict is reserved for require mode in P2. A token sent while mode is off gives status off with no verification. Keys that cannot be fetched give unverified, which is kept distinct from invalid. Only status valid yields a non-nil `identity.Subject` for p1-group-policy, p1-block-list and later per-user features. Every other status is treated as anonymous, so group- and user-scoped rules never match and default-deny holds. sub is the authoritative key for user rules, and email matching requires a verified email.
- Recording. `analytics.Event` gains `UserSub, UserEmail, UserGroups, UserGroupsTruncated, UserSID, IdentityStatus, IdentityReason` with explicit snake_case json tags and omitempty (Event has no tags today except UID). Unattributed events, receipts and sync payloads therefore stay byte-identical, and old receipts keep verifying because Receipt keeps the signed EventJSON bytes. Every proxy event is stored through one new `p.recordEvent(ci connIdentity, e analytics.Event)`, which stamps the identity fields. This covers serve.go, tls.go, http.go, grpc.go, ws.go and storeDeny; pre-CONNECT parse failures pass the zero connIdentity. decisionLog adds user_sub, identity_status, identity_reason and groups_count. Email and the group list appear in operational logs only at debug level. The raw token is never logged, stored, signed, put in an error body or passed to the judge or MCP gateway.
- Storage. The local SQLiteStore gets additive addColumnIfAbsent migrations for user_sub, user_email, user_groups (a JSON array, because LDAP DN group names contain commas), user_groups_truncated, user_sid, identity_status and identity_reason, plus an index on (user_sub, ts). The columns are added to insertColumns, the GetEvents scan and the GetOldestEventIDs SELECT and scan, which is the SyncWorker source. FleetSQLiteStore.migrate is a bare CREATE TABLE today, so the fleet side gets a new idempotent addColumnIfAbsent helper, the same columns and indexes, and extended StoreAggregatedEvent INSERT and GetEvents scans. Rollout order is CP first, then workers. A version mismatch drops or empties the fields and never errors.
- Observability. A nil-safe `(*Metrics).RecordIdentityVerify(result, reason)` registers the OTel counter `warden.identity.verify.total{result,reason}` with bounded labels; P2 extends this instrument and does not add a new one. `RecordJWKSFetch(result)` registers `warden.identity.jwks.fetch.total{result}`. Identity time is recorded in the existing `warden.request.added_latency` histogram with stage=identity. Budget: p99 under 100µs for a cached token, and under 1ms uncached excluding key fetches.
- Dashboard. `analytics.EventFilter.User` matches user_sub exactly or lower(user_email), using parameterized SQL only. It is exposed as `?user=` on /dashboard/api/traffic and /dashboard/api/analytics on worker and CP, and the analytics cache key includes the normalized user. Analytics adds a top-users table. The Query Builder schema already comes from PRAGMA table_info, so the user columns appear in it with no code change. index.html adds a user column and a filter box and renders claim values with textContent only.
- Deployment and docs. Workers need egress to the issuer for discovery and JWKS, so deploy/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml and the compose templates allow worker to issuer traffic. docs/control-plane.md documents the identity block, the per-agent field, the transport rules (X-Warden-Identity only with TLS termination; Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT works everywhere and is recommended) and the rollout order. They also state that a P1 identity is a bearer assertion signed by the IdP and not yet bound to the agent; P2 adds binding and bundle-distributed JWKS.

## Done when

On a real deployment (CP plus at least one worker with TLS termination, Dex from p1-dex) with an agent in attribute mode, a request with a valid Dex token produces a local event, a signed receipt, a decision log line and a CP fleet event. Each carries the user's sub, verified email and groups with identity_status=valid. This holds for Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT and for X-Warden-Identity, over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. The upstream never sees X-Warden-Identity or Proxy-Authorization on any terminated path, in any mode. Invalid, expired, conflicting and missing tokens, and tokens sent while Dex is unreachable, are recorded as invalid, expired, conflict, none and unverified respectively, have no policy subject, and are allowed. The worker starts and serves traffic with Dex down. warden.identity.verify.total reports each outcome. Existing warden.db and fleet DB files upgrade in place with no data loss, and existing receipts still verify.

### 1/7 · W-P1-VRFY-01

**Add internal/identity OIDC verifier with lazy JWKS, cache and config**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#21](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/21)

Create the new package internal/identity with Claims, Status/Reason, the Verifier interface, StripHeaders and an OIDC verifier on go-oidc v3. Construction is lazy and never blocks, so the verifier can be built when Dex is down. Warden enforces the refetch floor, the exp/nbf skew and the size limits itself, so attribution never depends on library defaults. Add the identity settings block (SettingsWire, local YAML and the per-agent field) with validation. Nothing is wired into the proxy yet, so merging changes no behaviour.

**Requirements**

- New package internal/identity: Claims{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, GroupsTruncated, SID (optional), Issuer, AZP, Nonce, IssuedAt, Expiry}, Subject{Sub, Email, EmailVerified, Groups, AgentID} and SubjectFrom(claims, status) *Subject, which returns nil for every status except valid, Status off|none|valid|invalid|expired|unverified|conflict, a bounded Reason set, Verify(ctx, raw, opts...) (Claims, Status, Reason), and StripHeaders(http.Header).
- NewOIDCVerifier(Config) on github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3 (new go.mod dependency, pinned; govulncheck stays clean). It allows only RS256 and ES256, checks iss exactly, checks that aud contains Audience, and checks azp against AllowedAZP when that list is set.
- Warden checks exp and nbf with ClockSkew (default 60s, max 5m) and rejects exp-iat above MaxTokenTTL (default 1h). It rejects tokens over 16 KiB with reason too_large before parsing. Confirm against the pinned go-oidc version which built-in time checks must be disabled.
- No network I/O at construction. Discovery and JWKS fetches are lazy and use a dedicated http.Client (Proxy=nil, a plain net.Dialer rather than the proxy SafeDialer so private-network issuers are reachable, 5s timeout, capped body, optional CA file). An unknown kid triggers at most one refetch per 30s (singleflight plus an interval floor), and the last good keyset is kept. A failure to obtain keys returns status unverified with reason jwks_unavailable.
- Groups come from GroupsClaim (default groups) and are sorted, de-duplicated and capped at 64 entries of 256 bytes, with GroupsTruncated set. Email is lowercased and kept only when email_verified is not false; EmailVerified is true only when the claim is literally true. A bounded LRU (10k entries) keyed by sha256(token) caches results until min(exp, now+5m), and exp is re-checked on every hit.
- Config: IdentitySettings{DefaultMode, Issuer, Audience, AllowedAZP, JWKSURL, GroupsClaim, ClockSkewSeconds, MaxTokenTTLSeconds, AllowInsecureIssuer} on SettingsWire (json identity, omitempty) and a local identity: YAML block. Add a new Identity string field to AgentSettings, AgentPolicy and rawAgent. Validation accepts off|attribute, rejects require with a Phase 2 error in the CP write path and local YAML (parseRemotePolicy on a worker does not reject a served wire for an unsupported mode; W-P1-VRFY-07 keeps the previous identity config, so a later CP that serves require never stalls P1 workers), and rejects http issuers unless AllowInsecureIssuer is set. DeepCopy and SettingsWireFromPolicy are extended. JSON and YAML keys are defaultMode, issuer, audience, allowedAZP, jwksURL, groupsClaim, clockSkewSeconds, maxTokenTTLSeconds and allowInsecureIssuer, and the per-agent key is `identity` on agents[]. allowedAZP has no built-in default (empty means no azp check); the reference configs and docs set [agent-harness, warden-cli].
- Raw tokens never appear in errors, logs or test output; only bounded reasons do. WithNonce(n) lets W-P1-SSO-03 reuse the verifier with its own audience.
- Add fakes.Verifier (map from token to Claims/Status/Reason, safe for concurrent use, counts calls) to test/fakes.
- For status expired and for invalid with reason bad_signature, wrong_iss, wrong_aud, wrong_azp, unknown_kid or ttl_too_long, Verify still returns the sub and email parsed from a well-formed payload, so W-P1-BLOCK-02 can deny on a match (a match can only deny). These claims never yield a Subject and are never cached as valid. malformed and too_large return empty Claims.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add go-oidc v3 to go.mod and create the new internal/identity/identity.go with Claims, Status, Reason, Verifier, VerifyOption/WithNonce and StripHeaders.
2. Add the new internal/identity/keyset.go: a rateLimitedKeySet wrapping the go-oidc remote key set (singleflight, 30s floor, last-good keys, Proxy=nil client, body cap), plus lazy discovery when JWKSURL is empty.
3. Add the new internal/identity/oidc.go: NewOIDCVerifier with algorithm allowlist, iss/aud/azp checks, Warden-side exp/nbf/TTL checks, size cap, groups and email normalisation, and an error-to-Reason mapping (errors.As on the go-oidc expiry error).
4. Add the new internal/identity/cache.go: a bounded LRU keyed by sha256(token) with expiry at min(exp, now+5m).
5. Add the new internal/config/identity.go with IdentitySettings, the local identity: block parsed through rawConfig, and validateIdentity. Add Identity to AgentSettings, AgentPolicy and rawAgent, and extend SettingsWireFromPolicy, its reverse projection and SettingsWire.DeepCopy in internal/config/settings.go.
6. Add fakes.Verifier to test/fakes/fakes.go.
7. Tests: the new internal/identity/oidc_test.go (httptest JWKS, RS256 and ES256 signers), keyset_test.go (rotation, refetch floor under -race, issuer down) and cache_test.go. Extend internal/config/settings_test.go with identity round-trip, DeepCopy and validation.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A valid token returns status valid with its Claims. Wrong iss, wrong aud, wrong azp, expired beyond 60s skew, nbf in the future, alg none, HS256 signed with the public key, exp-iat over 1h and a 17 KiB token each return the expected Status and Reason: `go test ./internal/identity -run TestOIDCVerifier`.
- [ ] After a JWKS rotation, a token with the new kid verifies after exactly one fetch, and 100 concurrent unknown-kid verifications within 30s cause at most one more fetch: `go test -race ./internal/identity -run TestJWKSRotation`.
- [ ] With the issuer unreachable, NewOIDCVerifier returns immediately, and Verify returns status unverified with reason jwks_unavailable within the context deadline.
- [ ] A group `cn=eng,ou=groups,dc=corp` survives intact, 100 groups are capped at 64 with GroupsTruncated=true, and email_verified=false leaves Email empty.
- [ ] A SettingsWire with an identity block and per-agent Identity round-trips byte-identically, a SettingsWire without one marshals with no identity key, and mode require fails with a Phase 2 message: `go test ./internal/config -run 'Identity'`.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including govulncheck with the new dependency.
- [ ] An expired token and a token signed by an unknown key return their sub in Claims with status expired and invalid respectively, and SubjectFrom returns nil for both; a valid token with email_verified absent keeps Email but has EmailVerified=false: `go test ./internal/identity -run 'TestUnverifiedClaims|TestSubjectFrom'`.

### 2/7 · W-P1-VRFY-02

**Extract, verify and strip identity on CONNECT, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#22](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/22)

Wire identity into the proxy. Capture Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT and X-Warden-Identity on terminated HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, verify both through a new identityP atomic holder, and carry the result on a per-connection connIdentity. Stripping must also run on the h2 path (handleGRPC/serveGRPCStream), because that path bypasses runRequestStages and copyGRPCHeaders forwards every other header. Attribute mode never blocks, and with no identity configured the only change is that the two headers are stripped.

**Requirements**

- A new identityP atomic.Pointer[identityHolder] on Proxy with identity() and SetIdentity(v, mode), mirroring secretsP, plus an optional Identity field on proxy.Config. A nil holder means mode off.
- handleConn captures Proxy-Authorization in the CONNECT header loop (Basic user session, or Bearer; any other form is invalid/malformed) and verifies it before Policy.Evaluate with a 2s context. The result is a connIdentity{Claims, Status, Reason, Expiry} passed to handleTLS, tunnel, handleHTTP and handleGRPC. connIdentity keeps the unverified sub and email that Verify returns for expired and invalid tokens, for the W-P1-BLOCK-02 deny check only.
- A new identityStage runs in runRequestStages after readRequest and before judgeGate. serveGRPCStream calls the same resolver before the secret swap and before copyGRPCHeaders. Both call identity.StripHeaders in every mode.
- Status rules: CONNECT identity re-checked against Expiry on every request (expired after exp plus skew). Header identity is used when CONNECT had none. Two valid identities with different sub give conflict, and the request proceeds. A token sent in mode off gives off, with no Verify call. Only valid yields a non-nil Subject on requestScope.
- New nil-safe (*Metrics).RecordIdentityVerify(result, reason) registers warden.identity.verify.total. Identity time is recorded in warden.request.added_latency with stage=identity.
- When mode is attribute and no CA is configured, log one warning at startup that only CONNECT identity is available. The raw token never reaches logs, events, the judge or the MCP gateway.
- Bound the CONNECT header loop in handleConn, which reads headers without any limit today: at most 32 KiB of header bytes and 100 lines (room for a 16 KiB token base64-encoded in Basic credentials) and a 10s read deadline that is cleared once the headers end. Overflow or timeout returns `431 Request Header Fields Too Large` (timeout just closes) and stores a deny event with reason `headers_too_large`, added to internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06).

**Implementation plan**

1. Add identityHolder, identityP, identity() and SetIdentity in internal/proxy/proxy.go, seeded from proxy.Config in New.
2. Add the new internal/proxy/identity.go with connIdentity, resolveConnIdentity(header value) and resolveRequestIdentity(ci, r *http.Request), which applies the status rules and calls identity.StripHeaders.
3. In internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn, read Proxy-Authorization in the header loop, build connIdentity before Policy.Evaluate, and pass it to handleTLS and tunnel. In internal/proxy/tls.go, pass it to handleHTTP and handleGRPC.
4. Add a connIdentity field and a Subject field to requestScope, and insert identityStage after readRequest in runRequestStages (internal/proxy/http.go).
5. In internal/proxy/grpc.go, pass connIdentity into serveGRPCStream and call resolveRequestIdentity at its top, before the swap and copyGRPCHeaders.
6. Add RecordIdentityVerify to internal/observability/observability.go and call it once per verification.
7. Tests: the new internal/proxy/identity_test.go (HTTP/1.1, WebSocket upgrade and h2 ALPN clients against a header-recording upstream, all modes, fakes.Verifier), a race test for SetIdentity, and BenchmarkIdentityStage next to http_bench_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] For HTTP/1.1, WebSocket upgrade and an h2 ALPN client, in mode off, with no settings and in attribute mode, the upstream never sees X-Warden-Identity or Proxy-Authorization: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityStripping`.
- [ ] In mode off with a token present, fakes.Verifier records zero calls and the resolved status is off.
- [ ] In attribute mode, invalid, expired, missing, unverifiable and conflicting tokens are all forwarded (200 from upstream) with status invalid, expired, none, unverified and conflict, a nil Subject, and a matching warden.identity.verify.total increment: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityAttributeMode`.
- [ ] A CONNECT identity whose exp passes during a keep-alive session gives status valid on the first request and expired on a request after exp plus skew.
- [ ] Concurrent SetIdentity swaps during traffic pass under `go test -race ./internal/proxy -run TestIdentityHotSwap`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/proxy -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkIdentityStage` shows the cached-token path under 100µs/op.
- [ ] A CONNECT with 40 KiB of headers gets 431 and one deny event with reason headers_too_large and no dial, while a CONNECT carrying a 16 KiB token in Proxy-Authorization is accepted: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestConnectHeaderBounds`.

### 3/7 · W-P1-VRFY-03

**Record user fields on worker events, receipts, decision logs and sync**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#23](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/23)

Worker side of recording. Add identity fields to analytics.Event with snake_case json tags and omitempty, so unattributed events, receipts and sync payloads stay byte-identical. Add the local SQLite columns, including in the GetOldestEventIDs read that feeds SyncWorker, and route every proxy event through one recordEvent helper that stamps the connection identity. The control-plane fleet store is handled in W-P1-VRFY-06.

**Requirements**

- analytics.Event gains UserSub, UserEmail, UserGroups []string, UserGroupsTruncated, UserSID, IdentityStatus and IdentityReason with json tags user_sub, user_email, user_groups, user_groups_truncated, user_sid, identity_status and identity_reason, all omitempty. Existing field names and tags are unchanged.
- The local SQLiteStore adds the seven columns through addColumnIfAbsent (TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '' / INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0), plus an index on (user_sub, ts). user_groups is stored as a JSON array, never comma-joined.
- insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, the GetEvents scan, and the GetOldestEventIDs SELECT and scan all carry the new columns, so the fields reach SyncWorker.
- Every proxy event goes through a new p.recordEvent(ci connIdentity, e analytics.Event), covering serve.go, tls.go, http.go, grpc.go, ws.go and storeDeny. Only pre-CONNECT parse failures use the zero connIdentity.
- decisionLog and logDecision add user_sub, identity_status, identity_reason and groups_count. Email and the group list are logged only at debug level, and the token never is.
- Receipts cover the fields automatically, because SigningStore signs the marshalled Event. Old receipts keep verifying.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the fields and json tags to Event in internal/analytics/analytics.go, plus new encodeGroups/decodeGroups (JSON) helpers.
2. Add the addColumnIfAbsent entries and the index in SQLiteStore migrate. Extend insertColumns, StoreEvent, StoreEventsBatch, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs.
3. Add recordEvent and connIdentity.stamp in internal/proxy/identity.go. Replace each direct analyticsStore().StoreEvent call in serve.go, tls.go, http.go, grpc.go and ws.go, and give storeDeny a connIdentity parameter.
4. Extend decisionLog and logDecision in internal/proxy/observe.go.
5. Tests: a migration test from a fixture warden.db without the columns (pattern of activity_columns_test.go), a golden marshal test for an identity-free Event, an internal/audit receipt test, a SyncWorker test that reads the fields from GetOldestEventIDs, and an AST test in internal/proxy.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An old warden.db with rows opens with the new columns added, old rows intact with defaults, and a second open is a no-op: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestMigrateUserColumns`.
- [ ] An identity-free Event marshals to the same bytes as before this change, and its receipt has no user_* keys. An attributed event's receipt contains "user_sub" and "identity_status":"valid" and audit.Verify passes: `go test ./internal/audit -run TestReceiptIdentityFields`.
- [ ] A group named `cn=eng,ou=groups,dc=corp` round-trips through StoreEvent, GetEvents and GetOldestEventIDs unchanged.
- [ ] An AST test fails if any non-test file in internal/proxy calls StoreEvent outside recordEvent: `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestAllEventsCarryIdentity`.
- [ ] A CONNECT to a denied host with a valid Proxy-Authorization token stores a deny event with the user's sub and status valid.
- [ ] Captured decision log output contains user_sub and identity_status and never the raw token.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-VRFY-02`](identity-verification.md#27--w-p1-vrfy-02) Extract, verify and strip identity on CONNECT, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2

### 4/7 · W-P1-VRFY-04

**Add user filter and top-users breakdown to the dashboard**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#24](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/24)

Let operators filter traffic and analytics by user on worker and CP dashboards. Add EventFilter.User across the local, central and fleet stores, expose ?user= on the traffic and analytics APIs (including the analytics cache key), and add a top-users table and a user column to the UI. The Query Builder schema already reads PRAGMA table_info, so the user columns appear there with no code change.

**Requirements**

- analytics.EventFilter gains User, matching user_sub exactly or lower(user_email) = lower(User), with parameterized SQL only. SQLiteStore, CentralStore and FleetSQLiteStore honor it (AggregatedFilter through embedding).
- /dashboard/api/traffic and /dashboard/api/analytics accept ?user= (at most 320 characters, otherwise 400). The handleAnalytics cache key includes the normalized user value.
- Analytics adds topUsers: the top 10 by request count with deny count, grouped by user_sub with the latest email for display, plus one unattributed bucket.
- index.html gets a user column (email, falling back to sub) and a filter box that sets ?user=. Claim values are rendered with textContent only.
- The filter uses the (user_sub, ts) index. The Query Builder needs no change; only a test covers it.
- With no identity data, responses are unchanged apart from an empty topUsers list.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add User to EventFilter in internal/analytics/analytics.go and apply it in SQLiteStore.GetEvents, CentralStore.GetEvents/GetAggregatedEvents (internal/analytics/central.go) and FleetSQLiteStore.GetEvents/GetAggregatedEvents.
2. In internal/dashboard/dashboard.go, parse and bound ?user= in handleTraffic and handleAnalytics, and add the user to the analytics cache key (currently range + proxy).
3. Add the topUsers aggregate to the analytics computation for both worker and fleet stores.
4. Add the user column and filter box to internal/dashboard/index.html.
5. Tests in internal/dashboard/dashboard_test.go and internal/analytics (filter, cache key, schema, topUsers).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With events for alice@corp and bob@corp in local and fleet stores, GET /dashboard/api/traffic?user=Alice@Corp returns 200 with only Alice's events on worker and CP, and ?user=<alice-sub> returns the same set: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestTrafficUserFilter`.
- [ ] After /dashboard/api/analytics?range=24h&user=alice is cached, the same call with user=bob returns Bob's figures.
- [ ] ?user= longer than 320 characters returns 400.
- [ ] GET /dashboard/api/query/schema lists user_sub and user_email, and POST /dashboard/api/query with `SELECT user_sub, count(*) FROM events GROUP BY user_sub` returns 200 with rows.
- [ ] topUsers has at most 10 entries sorted by count descending, plus an unattributed bucket.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-VRFY-03`](identity-verification.md#37--w-p1-vrfy-03) Record user fields on worker events, receipts, decision logs and sync; [`W-P1-VRFY-06`](identity-verification.md#67--w-p1-vrfy-06) Store user fields in the control-plane fleet store

### 5/7 · W-P1-VRFY-05

**Add identity attribution e2e test and a CI integration job**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#25](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/25)

Prove attribution end to end under the integration build tag. The default issuer is an in-process OIDC issuer that can mint valid, expired and wrong-audience tokens on demand, so CI does not depend on Docker. The Dex container runs only when WARDEN_IT_DEX=1, to cover a real Dex token with LDAP groups. CI has no integration job today, so this ticket adds one.

**Requirements**

- The test lives under //go:build integration in test/integration and compiles nothing without the tag.
- A new in-process OIDC issuer helper (httptest discovery plus JWKS plus RS256 signer) mints valid, expired and wrong-aud tokens. When WARDEN_IT_DEX=1, the W-P1-DEX-02 recipe additionally covers a real Dex token with groups, fetched with `scripts/dex-token.sh --raw` (W-P1-DEX-02) rather than a second token client.
- A worker started through startProxy with a CA and identity mode attribute covers valid, expired, wrong-aud and missing tokens, each via Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT and via X-Warden-Identity, over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, plus one raw-tunnel case with Proxy-Authorization only.
- One case runs with the issuer stopped, and expects status unverified and a successful request.
- Assertions cover event identity fields, upstream-observed headers, warden.identity.verify.total counts via an OTel manual reader, and receipts that verify with user_sub.
- A new integration job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `scripts/check.sh --integration`. Test output never prints token strings.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the new test/integration/oidc_issuer_test.go helper (discovery, JWKS, token minting).
2. Add the new test/integration/identity_test.go with the case table and a header-recording upstream.
3. Start the proxy via startProxy with fakes.FakeAnalyticsStore, a signing store and a manual metrics reader.
4. Add the WARDEN_IT_DEX=1 branch that uses the W-P1-DEX-02 compose recipe.
5. Add the integration job to .github/workflows/ci.yml.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] All cases return the upstream's 200, and IdentityStatus is valid, expired, invalid, none or unverified as expected: `go test -tags=integration ./test/integration -run TestIdentityAttribution`.
- [ ] No subtest observes Proxy-Authorization or X-Warden-Identity at the upstream.
- [ ] warden.identity.verify.total shows the expected count for each result after the run.
- [ ] With WARDEN_IT_DEX=1 and the identity recipe running, a Dex token for a seeded LDAP user produces an event whose UserGroups contains `eng`.
- [ ] The new CI integration job runs `scripts/check.sh --integration` green, and `go vet ./test/integration/...` without the tag does not compile the file.

### 6/7 · W-P1-VRFY-06

**Store user fields in the control-plane fleet store**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#228](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/228)

Control-plane half of recording, split from W-P1-VRFY-03 because conventions require separate worker and CP tickets. FleetSQLiteStore.migrate is a bare CREATE TABLE today with no way to add columns, so this ticket adds an idempotent addColumnIfAbsent helper. It then adds the identity columns and index and carries them through ingest, StoreAggregatedEvent and GetEvents. Old fleet DBs upgrade in place.

**Requirements**

- A new idempotent addColumnIfAbsent helper (PRAGMA table_info) on FleetSQLiteStore. It runs forward-only, add-only migrations after CREATE TABLE.
- Add user_sub, user_email, user_groups (JSON array), user_groups_truncated, user_sid, identity_status and identity_reason, plus an index on (user_sub, ts).
- Extend the StoreAggregatedEvent INSERT and the GetEvents and GetAggregatedEvents scans. Ingest and CentralStore pass the fields through unchanged.
- Old fleet DBs open with no data loss, and a second open is a no-op.
- Events from workers without identity fields store empty defaults without errors.
- Do not add the existing missing DLP and latency columns here; record that gap separately.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the new addColumnIfAbsent method and a migration list to FleetSQLiteStore.migrate in internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go.
2. Extend StoreAggregatedEvent, GetEvents and GetAggregatedEvents in fleet_sqlite.go, using the encodeGroups/decodeGroups helpers from W-P1-VRFY-03.
3. Check that the ingest handler and CentralStore (internal/analytics/central.go) decode the new json tags. Fix them if not.
4. Tests: a fleet migration test from a fixture DB, and a round-trip test from SyncWorker to the ingest handler to FleetSQLiteStore.GetEvents.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An old fleet DB with rows opens with the new columns, rows intact, and a second open is a no-op: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestFleetMigrateUserColumns`.
- [ ] An attributed event synced by SyncWorker into an ingest handler backed by FleetSQLiteStore comes back from GetEvents with identical user fields: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestSyncIdentityFields`.
- [ ] A group named `cn=eng,ou=groups,dc=corp` round-trips through the fleet store unchanged.
- [ ] An event without identity fields ingests and reads back with empty user fields.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-VRFY-03`](identity-verification.md#37--w-p1-vrfy-03) Record user fields on worker events, receipts, decision logs and sync

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-APPR-03`](policy-approvals.md#39--w-p2-appr-03) Replay fleet events against base and draft for each revision; [`W-P1-VRFY-04`](identity-verification.md#47--w-p1-vrfy-04) Add user filter and top-users breakdown to the dashboard; [`W-P2-WBND-08`](identity-enforcement.md#810--w-p2-wbnd-08) Store agent and token type fields in the CP fleet store

### 7/7 · W-P1-VRFY-07

**Wire the identity verifier into worker assembly, hot reload and deployment**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#229](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/229)

Connect the verifier to real workers. Build it from local config or the distributed SettingsWire, and resolve the per-agent mode with the agent ID that worker.defaultAgentID already computes. Swap it through SettingsApplier without a restart. Also open worker egress to the issuer in the deploy templates and document the identity block, the transport rules and the rollout order. Mode stays off unless configured.

**Requirements**

- Worker assembly (internal/worker/worker.go) builds the verifier from pol.Identity and calls proxy SetIdentity. The mode comes from the matching Agents entry's Identity, then Identity.DefaultMode, then off, keyed by defaultAgentID.
- SettingsApplier.Apply rebuilds the verifier only when issuer, audience, JWKS URL, azp, skew or TTL settings change. Otherwise it only updates the mode.
- A rebuild failure, or an unknown mode from a newer CP, keeps the previous identity config and logs one warning without token data.
- deploy/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml and the compose templates allow worker egress to the issuer, documented as an operator-set value.
- docs/control-plane.md documents the identity block, the per-agent Identity field, the rule that X-Warden-Identity needs TLS termination while Proxy-Authorization on CONNECT works everywhere, the rule that sub is authoritative and email matching needs a verified email, the recommended `allowedAZP: [agent-harness, warden-cli]` for the reference Dex clients, and the CP-first rollout order.
- Worker startup never contacts the issuer, so a worker with Dex down still starts.

**Implementation plan**

1. In internal/worker/worker.go, build the verifier with identity.NewOIDCVerifier and resolve the mode using defaultAgentID (internal/worker/judge.go).
2. In internal/worker/applier.go, compare the previous and new identity settings, then rebuild or update the mode and call SetIdentity.
3. Update deploy/k8s/networkpolicy.yaml and the compose templates under deploy/compose for issuer egress.
4. Update docs/control-plane.md.
5. Tests in internal/worker/applier_test.go and a worker assembly test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a SettingsWire whose Agents entry for this worker sets Identity=attribute and DefaultMode off, Apply activates verification without a restart: `go test ./internal/worker -run TestSettingsApplierIdentity`.
- [ ] An Apply that changes only an unrelated setting keeps the same verifier instance, and an issuer change replaces it.
- [ ] An unknown mode keeps the previous config and logs one warning.
- [ ] A worker configured with an unreachable issuer starts and serves traffic in its test.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including any manifest validation.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-VRFY-02`](identity-verification.md#27--w-p1-vrfy-02) Extract, verify and strip identity on CONNECT, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
